channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iranian Officials Report New US Strikes on Qeshm Island
item.description: Iranian officials confirmed new US attacks on Qeshm Island last night. The deputy governor of Hormozgan province stated that the strikes did not result in human casualties and caused no damage to vital infrastructure. Residents reported hearing explosions. This marks at least the third US attack on the island in under a week.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Explains Rationale Behind Land Allocation Restrictions
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov urged citizens needing housing to queue for apartments via the State Mortgage Company instead of requesting land for private homes. He cited the scarcity of flat land in Kyrgyzstan, which is 94% mountainous, and the need to preserve agricultural land and pastures for future generations. He noted that 4,950 apartments are under construction in Kara-Balta, with over 3,000 remaining after current queues are filled.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Enhance Control Over Drug Sales from 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to strengthen state control over the circulation of medicines and medical devices starting January 1, 2027. The Ministry of Health has developed draft regulations to revise risk assessment criteria and inspection checklists. Special attention will be given to unlicensed sales, unregistered, counterfeit, or substandard drugs, and the dispensing of narcotics and potent substances without prescriptions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Foils Smuggling Attempt Worth Over 2.1 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's border guards prevented the illegal movement of goods and cargo worth over 2.1 billion tenge in October 2026. The National Security Committee reported that 1,267 instances of illegal border crossings were thwarted, along with 119 poaching incidents in the Caspian Sea, resulting in the seizure of sturgeon.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Audit Water Management Facilities Built with ARIS Support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will audit water supply and sanitation facilities constructed under projects by the Agency for Development and Investment of Communities (ARIS). Concerns have been raised about unfinished or poorly maintained projects. A special commission will review facilities built in the last five years.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Resolution of Land Dispute for Migrant's Family
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the resolution of a land dispute concerning a house in the village of Intymak, Jyl District. The house was built with funds sent by the resident's son and daughter-in-law, who worked as labor migrants in Russia for 12 years. A legal dispute arose five years after construction.

item.title: Modern "Nukus city" housing complex to be built for 50,000 residents
item.description: A modern "Nukus city" housing complex will be built in Nukus, Uzbekistan, on 270 hectares, designed for 50,000 residents. The project will utilize advanced architectural solutions and energy-saving technologies, incorporating smart city features, green spaces, and social facilities. Construction will prioritize renewable energy and climate-adaptive design.

item.title: Bishkek Hospitals Suspend Partnered Births Due to Facility and Staffing Issues
item.description: State maternity hospitals in Bishkek are currently not offering partnered births, despite Kyrgyz law not prohibiting them. The Ministry of Health cited insufficient individual delivery rooms, facility layouts, high staff workload, and the need for patient privacy and safety as reasons for the suspension.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Provide Clean Water to 150 Villages Annually Starting 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, Kyrgyzstan plans to supply clean drinking water to 150 villages each year. This announcement came during a meeting where residents raised concerns about unfinished water projects. The goal is to significantly increase the number of villages with access to safe water.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA: Children Poisoned in Tashkent Tournament Recovered Fully
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the situation involving Kazakh children poisoned at a football tournament in Tashkent was not as severe as initially perceived. All affected children have returned home after receiving treatment in Uzbekistan. The ministry thanked Uzbek medics and confirmed no long-term health damage.

item.title: Petition for Kazakh Activist Sanzhar Bokaev Garners Over 2,000 Signatures Abroad
item.description: The France-based Association "Human Rights in Central Asia" launched a petition for detained Kazakh activist Sanzhar Bokaev, collecting over 2,000 signatures internationally. The petition urges Kazakhstan's authorities to ensure a fair trial and prevent the use of criminal prosecution for peaceful activism and expression.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Gas Sector Faces Scrutiny Over Billions in Financial Irregularities
item.description: Auditors have uncovered financial irregularities totaling 24.1 billion tenge within Kazakhstan's gas industry. Despite significant gas reserves, the sector struggles to meet domestic demand, with issues including reliance on a few subsoil users and inconsistent gas quality affecting infrastructure and export potential.

item.title: Uzbekistan Fines 12 Bloggers for Advertising Law Violations
item.description: Uzbekistan's competition committee has fined 12 bloggers for violating advertising laws. The committee is expanding its monitoring of social media advertising, including content from popular artists and athletes. They emphasize that ignorance of advertising regulations does not exempt individuals from responsibility.

item.title: New Director Appointed to Almaty School After 58 Students Fell Ill
item.description: A new director has been appointed to the Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty, where 58 students were hospitalized with suspected intestinal infections. Almaz Kunkhozhin, who previously led the school, has taken over. Investigations found E. coli bacteria in food samples, leading to administrative protocols.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Review University Rectors' Performance and Address Graduate Unemployment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Education and Science will review the performance of state university rectors. The review will also address issues like graduate unemployment, outdated textbooks, and dormitory construction delays. Rectors must resolve identified shortcomings and organize student consultations within set deadlines.

item.title: Kazakhstan Undertakes Reconstruction of 746 Water Canals
item.description: Kazakhstan is currently undertaking the reconstruction of 746 water canals across the country. This initiative aims to improve water management and distribution infrastructure. The project is part of broader efforts to enhance agricultural productivity and ensure water security.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Return of Family Home to Owners
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the return of a family home to its owners in the Jайл district. The house was mistakenly transferred to municipal ownership due to incomplete registration in 2004. The president instructed relevant authorities to legalize the property and return it to the family.

item.title: Taliban Deputy PM Urges UN Cooperation on Jobs and Shelter for Returnees
item.description: Taliban Deputy Prime Minister Abdul Salam Hanafi met with UNAMA head Fatemeh Rabab, requesting cooperation in creating jobs and shelter for returning refugees. Hanafi stated over eight million refugees have returned to Afghanistan. Rabab acknowledged the challenges of managing returnees and pledged expanded UN efforts in job creation and aid distribution.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes Four Cars and 103 Million Tenge from Illegal Online Casino Operators
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Financial Monitoring has concluded an investigation into individuals organizing money transfers to illegal foreign online casinos, sending the criminal case to court. The total volume of illegal operations reached 191 billion tenge. Suspects used payment systems of three companies under their control, involving hundreds of payment terminals.

item.title: Central Asian Citizens Fall Victim to Drug Trafficking Schemes, Facing Severe Penalties Abroad
item.description: This article details real stories of Central Asian citizens whose lives were ruined by misplaced trust and excessive politeness, leading them to become unwitting drug couriers. Cases from Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan highlight individuals facing long prison sentences, including life imprisonment and even the death penalty, after being tricked into carrying drugs hidden in luggage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Review of Twin Brothers' Detention After Traffic Accident
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the Interior Ministry to investigate the detention of twin brothers held as passengers after a traffic accident. A resident appealed to the president, stating his nephews were passengers and not involved in the crash, questioning their imprisonment.

item.title: Russia to Restrict Migrant Employment in Taxis and Delivery Services in Eight Regions
item.description: Russia plans to restrict the employment of migrants in taxi services starting in 2027 across eight regions. Additionally, the Kaluga region will prohibit their involvement in courier activities. These measures are part of a draft government decree on the permissible share of foreign workers, prepared by the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection.

item.title: Eurasian Economies Week Review: Armenia Raises Rates, Kazakhstan Inflation Slows, Belarus Reserves Drop
item.description: The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) released its weekly macroeconomic review covering Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Uzbekistan. Key events include Armenia's central bank raising its key rate to 7%, a further slowdown in Kazakhstan's inflation, a decrease in Belarus's foreign exchange reserves, and growth in Russia's oil and gas revenues.

item.title: Kandahar Singers Face Hardship and Humiliation Under Taliban Rule
item.description: Singers in Kandahar report facing severe economic difficulties and humiliation by the Taliban, who reportedly call them "brothers of Satan." Banned from artistic activities, many artists have left the country. Those remaining struggle to earn a living, with some resorting to street vending. Musical instruments are confiscated and destroyed.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Restores Minor's Right to Receive Survivor's Benefit
item.description: The Transport Prosecutor's Office in Kyrgyzstan has restored the right of an orphaned minor, a student at the Kyrgyz Aviation Institute, to receive a survivor's benefit. The office identified a violation of the student's legal entitlement to the benefit and took measures to rectify the situation, ensuring she receives the due payments.

item.title: Drug Network Dismantled in Tashkent and Tashkent Region, Over 26,000 Doses Seized
item.description: Law enforcement agencies in Uzbekistan have dismantled a drug trafficking network in Tashkent and the Tashkent region. During several operations, approximately 26,300 doses of drugs, including hashish, mephedrone, and opium extract, were seized from suspects. The operations were part of the 'Safe and Healthy Country' campaign.

item.title: Suspected Cattle Rustling Group Arrested in Ekibastuz
item.description: Police in Ekibastuz have arrested a group of four individuals suspected of a series of cattle thefts, reportedly stealing around 40 head of small livestock. The suspects, residents of the region, allegedly carried out thefts systematically over several months. The Ministry of Internal Affairs stated that the investigation is ongoing to determine their involvement in other similar crimes.

item.title: Kazakh Businessman Claims $200,000 Lost in Kyrgyzstan Due to Alleged Fraud
item.description: A Kazakh businessman, Alidzhi Afarov, told Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov he lost over $200,000 when purchasing a quarry in the Chuy region. Afarov alleges one of the accused fraudsters posed as the president's nephew. President Japarov has instructed the Interior Ministry to investigate and recover the funds.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Real Estate Prices: Apartment and House Costs in September
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Agency for Land Resources, Cadastre, Geodesy, and Cartography released September 2026 data on average real estate prices per square meter. Bishkek leads in residential houses, apartments, and commercial properties. Detached houses in the capital averaged 173,242.6 som per square meter.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Host International Startup Competition with $5 Million Prize Fund Annually from 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, Uzbekistan will annually host the international "Land of Startups" competition, aiming to attract foreign projects, support technology transfer, and establish a regional startup hub. The Ministry of Digital Technologies announced the $5 million prize fund. The first competition in April will cover AI, digital social technologies, fintech, gaming, and B2B solutions.

item.title: SCO Energy Strategy Presented at UN Forum on Sustainable Energy for Development
item.description: The SCO's energy strategy was presented at the 15th UN International Forum on Energy for Sustainable Development in Xi'an, China. The SCO delegation, led by Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmuродзода, highlighted cooperation approaches and the Strategy for Developing Energy Cooperation until 2030. Two statements from the SCO Heads of State Council were also presented.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Imposes Potato Import Ban Amidst Farmer Concerns
item.description: A Kyrgyz lawmaker has raised concerns about low potato purchase prices in the Issyk-Kul region, impacting local farmers. The government has banned potato imports and is negotiating with Uzbekistan for potential exports, though VAT remains a sticking point.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Probe into Illegal Land and Property Privatization
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into the legality of land and property privatization in the Ak-Suu village, Moscow district. If violations are found, the property must be returned to municipal ownership. He also addressed issues with a stalled clean water project.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Demands Explanation for $25 Million Fuel Subsidy Spending
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan has demanded an explanation for the use of over $25 million allocated for subsidized fuel for farmers. The funds were channeled through a state bank to a private company. The MP questioned the high cost of fuel despite the subsidy and requested details on how the money was spent. The head of the State Material Reserves stated that subsidies were not received and fuel is sold at market prices, with state reserves offering lower prices.

item.title: G7 Foreign Ministers Convene in Paris to Discuss Ukraine Peace and Iran Tensions
item.description: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in Paris to discuss ending the war in Ukraine and preventing escalation involving Iran. The talks also cover broader international security concerns. European nations aim to ensure credible security guarantees for Kyiv in any peace agreement.

item.title: Tashkent to Become Tourism Capital of the Turkic World in 2027
item.description: Tashkent has been awarded the status of Tourism Capital of the Turkic World for 2027. The symbolic key was handed over to Uzbekistan at a ceremony in Istanbul. Ankara will hold this title in 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen ties between Turkic states.

item.title: Tajikistan Introduces Fines for Illegal Bank Card and E-Wallet Transfers
item.description: Tajikistan has introduced administrative penalties for the illegal transfer, sale, acquisition, and distribution of payment cards, e-wallets, and related information for mercenary purposes. A new article in the Code of Administrative Offenses imposes fines and confiscation of items used in the offense. Citizens are urged not to share SIM cards or payment details.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Means-Testing for Certain Social Benefits from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will gradually implement means-testing for specific social payments and benefits. This will affect 10 types of aid, including child birth and care, multi-child families, disability, and survivor benefits. Payments will be suspended for citizens deemed wealthy or with high well-being levels.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches $20 Billion Platform for Green Energy Transition
item.description: Kazakhstan is launching an investment platform, QaJET, aimed at attracting approximately $20 billion for its energy transition. The platform, set to officially launch on November 10 during COP31 in Antalya, will focus on renewable energy development, grid modernization, energy storage, and electrification. Funding will come from diverse national and international sources.

item.title: Tajikistan and EU Discuss Cooperation in Energy, Transport, and Industry
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon met with EU Commissioner for International Partnerships, Josef Sikele, to discuss cooperation. Key areas included energy, economy, transport, investment, and climate change resilience. Both sides emphasized strengthening ties within the 'Central Asia-European Union' format, noting its strategic partnership status.
